This is the first bail application filed by the applicant under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. for grant of regular bail, as he has been arrested in connection with Crime No. 170/2023 registered at Police Station - Jainagar, District - Surajpur, Chhattisgarh for the offences punishable under Section 363,
366-A, 376 of I.P.C. 1860 and under Section 4 of Prevention of Children from Sexual Offences, Act,
2012.
2.

sentences.text: Case of the prosecution is that, on 05.08.2023, victim went to school, however, she did not return back to her house.
She was searched and when, whereabouts of the victim was not traced, F.I.R. was registered against an unknown person for the alleged commission of offence under Section 363 of I.P.C.

Victim was recovered on 07.08.2023, her statement was recorded under Section 161 of Cr.P.C.
and the aforementioned offences were also added in the
F.I.R.
Applicant was arrested on 28.08.2023.
3. Learned counsel for the applicant submits that applicant has been falsely implicated in the instant case and he has not committed any offence as alleged.

He submits that during trial, victim and her Rajesh Kumar Giddh vs State Of Chhattisgarh on 17 January, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/95035663/
1 father were examined before the Trial Court and they have not supported the case of the prosecution.

entities.label: PRECEDENT

sentences.text: He has placed in record the copy of deposition of the victim and deposition of her father.
Therefore, he may be enlarged on regular bail.

4. On the other hand, learned State counsel opposes the submission made by learned counsel for the applicant and submits that serious allegations are leveled against the applicant by victim in her statement recorded under Section 161 and 164 of Cr.P.C.
He further submits that the deposition of the victim and her father, relied upon by the counsel for the applicant is subject matter of appreciation by the Trial Court.

5. Pursuant to the notice issued by this Court, victim along with her mother is present before this Court through virtual mode from D.L.S.A. Surajpur, District - Surajpur and she has raised no objection in grant of bail to the applicant.
6.
I have heard learned counsel for the respective parties.

7. Taking in consideration the facts and circumstances of the case, nature of allegations, submission of counsel for the applicant based on the deposition of the victim and her father and further considering the submission of the victim present before this Court along with her mother, without commenting on the merits of the case, I am inclined to allow this application for grant of bail.

8. Accordingly, the bail application filed under Section 439 of Cr.P.C. is allowed and it is directed that applicant shall be released on bail on his furnishing a personal bond in the sum of Rs. 25,000/-
with one surety in the like sum to satisfaction of Trial Court concerned on the conditions that:
(i) He shall appear before the Trial Court concerned regularly on each and every date unless exempted from appearance.
(ii) He shall not, in any manner, tamper with the prosecution witnesses.
(iii) If applicant is found involved in similar offence in future, it will be open for the State to apply for cancellation of bail.
9.
Certified copy as per rules.
